title: Willie Jones and early jazz fiddle in New Orleans
summary: A boyhood friend, Willie Jones, played jazz fiddle and showed the others the extra notes. Jimmy Palao is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: But you tried to play jazz yourself, any of these boys that you knew, studying music?

Yes, we had one boy that, he was better than all of us. He had a darn good ear, and he played a few of those ragged notes on the fiddle, and he showed us how to do them, and he said he was playing this big melody, and all the tunes that were out then.
Do you remember the names of any of those kids?

Willie Jones was the boy that played the kind of a jazz fiddle. Did he ever get with a band? He was with several bands down there, but he never got really famous or nothing like that, because I know he played with different bands around there, but the fiddle wasn't much of an instrument in those days.
I think by that time, Paloa, was that his name?
